declared_purpose: Manage Asana workspaces, projects and tasks, including search, creation, updates, completion and comments. PAT-first authentication is recommended; OAuth is optional. These capabilities are explicit; field selections, credential persistence and request construction are implementation choices (SKILL.md:3-3,15-26,53-76; README.md:3-12).

data_operations.operation: Read local configuration and resolve authentication
data_operations.source: CLI arguments, environment and local JSON files
data_operations.data_scope: PAT, OAuth access/refresh tokens, client credentials and default workspace. main reads config.json even when --token is supplied; authentication prefers --token, ASANA_PAT, config PAT, then token.json.
data_operations.condition: CLI execution; OAuth token loading occurs only when no direct token or PAT resolves. Refresh credentials come from flags.client_id/flags.client_secret or environment.

data_operations.operation: Persist PAT or default workspace locally
data_operations.source: CLI arguments, ASANA_PAT and existing configuration
data_operations.data_scope: PAT or default_workspace_gid, preserving existing configuration properties
data_operations.condition: configure.mjs PAT mode, asana_api.mjs set-pat, or set-default-workspace. The workspace command resolves authentication before saving.
clear-pat; other properties remain. This does not remove environment credentials, OAuth files or revoke credentials remotely.

data_operations.source: CLI arguments or ASANA_CLIENT_ID and ASANA_CLIENT_SECRET
data_operations.condition: configure.mjs --mode oauth with both credentials available

data_operations.operation: Construct and return an OAuth authorization URL
data_operations.source: CLI/environment client ID, optional scope/state and generated state
data_operations.data_scope: Client ID, OOB redirect URI, response type, state and explicit scope when supplied
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output to the caller; https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_authorize only if the URL is opened
data_operations.condition: oauth_oob.mjs authorize; the script prints instructions and does not itself open the browser or fetch this URL. Default scope omits the scope parameter.

data_operations.source: CLI authorization code and CLI/environment client credentials
data_operations.data_scope: Authorization code, client ID, client secret, grant type and OOB redirect URI
data_operations.condition: oauth_oob.mjs token with required inputs; supports the optional OAuth authentication purpose

data_operations.source: Loaded OAuth token and CLI/environment client credentials
data_operations.data_scope: Refresh token, client ID, client secret and refresh grant type
data_operations.condition: OAuth fallback with a refresh token when expiry is absent or within two minutes; requires client credentials. This also runs before local set-default-workspace when these conditions hold.

data_operations.operation: Persist OAuth responses and derived expiry metadata
data_operations.source: Successful token exchange or refresh response
data_operations.data_scope: Entire response object plus obtained_at_ms and calculated expires_at_ms; refresh also preserves prior token properties
data_operations.condition: Successful OAuth exchange or refresh; exact returned fields are not defined by the supplied source

data_operations.operation: Read Asana account, workspace and project data
data_operations.data_scope: me and workspaces return server-selected fields; projects requests workspace-filtered gid, name, resource_type, archived and public by default, with caller-overridable fields and limit
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Bearer credential and query parameters go to https://app.asana.com/api/1.0; responses return through standard output to the caller

data_operations.operation: Read task lists and task details
data_operations.data_scope: Project or assignee filters and task fields, including names, completion, assignees, dates, links and modification times; task detail additionally requests notes and project/section names. opt_fields and list limits are configurable.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Authenticated requests to https://app.asana.com/api/1.0; responses return through standard output to the caller
data_operations.condition: tasks-in-project, tasks-assigned or task; tasks-assigned defaults to self and completed_since=now

data_operations.operation: Resolve self-assignment through an additional account read
data_operations.data_scope: Unrestricted response requested; only data.gid is consumed to resolve the current account
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Asana API receives the authenticated request; response remains in the local process
data_operations.condition: tasks-assigned with default/explicit me, or search-tasks with --assignee me

data_operations.operation: Search tasks using forwarded CLI flags
data_operations.data_scope: Search text, filters and almost all other flags, including authentication flags if supplied; assignee/project aliases are transformed. Default response fields include task names, completion, assignee names, due dates and links.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: URL query at https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/workspaces/{workspace}/tasks/search; response returns through standard output
data_operations.condition: search-tasks; only _, assignee, project and opt_fields are removed from the initial flag copy before request construction

data_operations.operation: Send task mutations and return their results
data_operations.data_scope: Updates: name, notes, due date or completion; completion: completed=true; comments: text; creation: name, notes and optional workspace, projects and due date
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Authenticated POST/PUT requests to Asana task/story endpoints; responses return to the caller
data_operations.condition: update-task, complete-task, comment or create-task after required-input checks. Server-side retention and visibility are unspecified.

data_operations.source: Asana API or OAuth token endpoint responses
data_operations.data_scope: Entire parsed error response, or up to 300 characters of a non-JSON response, included in an error/stack
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard error to the invoking caller
data_operations.condition: Remote HTTP failure or non-JSON response; no additional logging recipient is implemented here

data_operations.operation: Interpret chat input locally and return command arguments
data_operations.data_scope: Normalized input; slash-command arguments, inferred command/self-assignment intent and extracted date range
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output to the caller; this helper does not execute the generated API command
data_operations.condition: Optional chat helper invocation; unmatched text returns unknown

potential_excess.data_scope: Authentication flags such as token, client_secret/client-secret and client_id/client-id, plus unrelated CLI flags
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Asana task-search URL query, beyond the required bearer header or OAuth token endpoint
potential_excess.condition: search-tasks invoked with these flags; environment credentials alone are not copied into the query
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Task search requires search criteria and authenticated access; copying all CLI flags is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Authenticate the request and transmit the requested task-search filters.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Separate authentication/control flags from search parameters and forward only supported search filters. This removes extra data from a required request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain documented search filters, field selection and limits, and preserve the existing bearer-authentication path.

potential_excess.data_scope: OAuth client ID and client secret
potential_excess.condition: configure.mjs --mode oauth; no supplied authentication component reads this file
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Optional OAuth setup is declared and storage is documented, but this credential copy does not feed the packaged OAuth exchange or refresh paths.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Make client credentials available to OAuth exchange/refresh through their implemented flags or environment inputs.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the unused credential-file write from the packaged setup flow and use the existing direct inputs. This removes redundant persistence.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Update setup instructions consistently; preserve explicit credential persistence only if a separately required consumer is established.

potential_excess.data_scope: OAuth refresh token and client credentials; refreshed token response
potential_excess.condition: set-default-workspace with OAuth fallback requiring refresh
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Saving a caller-provided default workspace is a local configuration operation; it does not use an access token.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Persist default_workspace_gid while preserving the other configuration properties.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Handle set-default-workspace before resolving bearer authentication. This removes a redundant refresh action and token rewrite from that path.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep authentication and refresh for commands that actually call Asana.

potential_excess.data_scope: Any /users/me response fields beyond data.gid, if returned
potential_excess.condition: Self-assignee resolution for tasks-assigned or search-tasks
potential_excess.purpose_basis: This internal lookup consumes only the current account GID; other returned account fields have no demonstrated use on this path.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Resolve me to the correct account GID.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Request only gid if the endpoint supports field selection. This narrows data in a required lookup rather than assuming the lookup can be removed.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Verify endpoint support and preserve correct self-assignee resolution. Actual default response fields are unresolved.

unknowns: Asana-side retention, query logging, sharing, deletion and exact response fields are undocumented here; remote disclosure does not establish those later operations.
Actual OAuth grants when scope is omitted are unknown. The reference lists scope examples, while authorize omits scope by default (references/asana-endpoints.md:19-20; scripts/oauth_oob.mjs:90-101).
Token-response field contents are unknown, so excess fields persisted by whole-response copying cannot be identified conclusively (scripts/oauth_oob.mjs:124-130; scripts/asana_api.mjs:131-138).
Support for selecting only gid on /users/me remains unverified; this blocks confirming the proposed field reduction.
External wrappers, consumers of credentials.json, caller-side output retention, filesystem permissions and storage protections are outside the supplied source.

End-to-end OAuth setup has source inconsistencies: README documents auth-url although the helper dispatches authorize/token; API refresh reads underscore credential flags despite documenting hyphenated flags (README.md:25-25; scripts/oauth_oob.mjs:90-134; scripts/asana_api.mjs:10-11,156-159).
